before_native_call: Retain exact libc/loader files and derived image biases; validate current loaded backing/ranges at the same stable-loader boundary as FloatingEnvironment. Do not use CDLL/dlsym as address authentication.
Verify complete GNU verneed/verdef joins, including required ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 and GLIBC_PRIVATE. Existing MuJoCo unversioned-symbol policy remains unchanged.

Validate libc GLOB_DAT slots0x219ec8 and0x219fa0 against expected loader symbol starts, and loader RELATIVE slot0x39e48 against loader bias+0x14d80. Native observed targets are evidence to compare with those expectations, never the expectations themselves.

Validate selected code ranges and profile body bytes from pinned files; where existing policy checks current instruction bytes, use exact nonrelocated body bytes retained here. Check object extents before reading slot or mutex metadata.

Read the source-fixed mutex kind (must equal1), and refuse the exact counter-overflow state. Do not copy/restore shared glibc mutex bytes; allow its maintained synchronization and private futex wait/wake.

Enter fenv preservation before metadata/guard work. Use a retained owned callback with exact source/DWARF ABI and keep callback lifetime through synchronous return. Catch callback errors explicitly and stop safely.

Require callback size covers all fields before copying primitive values. Do not dereference dlpi_name merely to identify the module: compare authenticated load bias and program-header identity. Do not retain native struct views after callback.

If the target module has absent/unallocated TLS or is not enumerated in the callback namespace, retain unresolved/refuse before MuJoCo getters/copy/query. Never call __tls_get_addr, a getter, or a query to initialize as a transparent fallback.

Use the prior exact five-array profile to validate/copy/restore current-thread producer TLS bytes, preserving opaque pointers as bytes. Keep adapter/scratch reentry protection and poison after failed restore.
Retain terminal/cancellation branches and declared OS/bridge assumptions; this is no whole-libc, loader, TLS, process-state or performance certification.
